chunks: Dawud al-Sarmi asked Abā al-Ḥasan ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad عليه السلام and said to him:
I go out on this route, and sometimes there is no place for me to perform salat (prayer) except because of the snow, so how should I act?
He said: "If you can avoid performing sajdah on the snow, then do not perform sajdah on it. But if that is not possible for you, then level it and perform sajdah on it."

key_terms.الثَّلْجِ: snow, the surface under discussion for sajdah
key_terms.فَسَوِّهِ: then level it or smooth it out
key_terms.مَوْضِعٌ: a place or spot suitable for prayer

ai.seo_question: How should one perform sajdah during salat when praying on snow is unavoidable?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding performing sajdah when a person is in snowy conditions and cannot find another suitable place for salat (prayer). Imam ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad al-Hādī عليه السلام instructs that one should avoid sajdah on snow if possible, but if there is no alternative, the snow may be leveled and sajdah performed on it.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.802 - Dawud Al-Sarmi asked Abu Al-Hasan Imam Ali ibn Muhammad Al-Hadi (as) about going on a journey where there may be no place to pray except on snow.
How should he pray in such a case?
Imam (as) replied: "If you can avoid prostrating on the snow, then do not prostrate on it. But if it is not possible, then level it and prostrate on it."
